How to read these numbers. The ESPN spread shows the team ESPN expects to win and by how many points, with a minus sign: Utah −3.0 means ESPN has Utah winning by 3.0. KickTip's expected margin is our own number from the model: the team KickTip expects to win and by how many points, for example “Utah by 3.5” (rounded to 0.5 on the page). The ESPN spread is shown with the time it was read (MT) and only when ESPN has posted one. Neither number is a recommendation. Information only.

How Big 12 ties are broken

When two teams finish tied in conference play, Big 12 applies these steps in order until one team is ahead:

  1. Head-to-head result between the two teams
  2. Record against all common conference opponents
  3. Record against the highest-placed common opponent in the standings, then the next, and so on
  4. Combined conference win percentage of each team's conference opponents
  5. Total wins in a 12-game season
  6. Ranking-based step (CFP rank, computer composite or similar): KickTip uses its rating as a stand-in
  7. Random draw (coin toss)

Ties among three or more teams use a similar list, starting with results among the tied teams. This is a plain-English summary of the official policy; the official text controls.

Known limitations

  • The step that relies on other public rating systems is replaced by KickTip's rating; the coin toss is modeled as a random draw.
  • 'Total wins in a 12-game season' counts at most one FCS win; NCAA-exempt games are ignored.
  • KickTip uses the official Big 12 policy labeled 2024-present (republished Nov. 4, 2025).
